title: Strong resolvent convergence and spectral limits
subtitle: A topology for changing domains and unbounded spectra
adaptation: Mathematical companion outlining the definitions, argument, worked cases, and scope of the source lecture.

slides.title: Which convergence survives unboundedness?
slides.lead: Comparing the operators directly may require incompatible domains.
body: Instead compare their inverses at a common nonreal spectral parameter. Each resolvent is bounded and is defined throughout the Hilbert space.

slides.title: Strong, norm, and resolvent convergence
slides.lead: The vector is fixed before taking a strong limit.
body: Operator-norm convergence controls every unit vector simultaneously. Strong convergence allows discrepancies at moving high-frequency vectors. Resolvent convergence works even with changing operator domains.

slides.title: Multiplication by an unbounded diagonal
slides.lead: Let A act on the n-th coordinate by n.
body: Its symmetric Yosida approximant replaces large eigenvalues by bounded multipliers. For fixed n the multipliers tend to n, but the convergence is not uniform over all n.

slides.title: Convergence of diagonal resolvents
slides.lead: For each fixed coordinate, the shifted inverse converges.
body: Each resolvent multiplier has modulus at most one. Applied to a fixed square-summable vector, dominated convergence of the squared coordinate errors yields strong resolvent convergence.

slides.title: Why resolvent-norm convergence fails
slides.lead: High frequencies defeat a uniform estimate.
body: For fixed R and n much larger than R squared, the approximated eigenvalue is near zero. Its resolvent is near i, while the original resolvent tends to zero. The operator-norm difference stays large.

slides.title: Graph convergence from resolvents
slides.lead: Resolvents produce compatible approximating domain vectors.
body: Put y_n=(A_n-iI)^{-1}x. Then y_n converges to y, and A_n y_n=x+i y_n converges to Ay. Both coordinates of graph points converge.

slides.title: Continuous spectral functions
slides.lead: A bounded continuous function respects strong resolvent limits.
body: Strong resolvent convergence of self-adjoint operators transfers to strong convergence of their bounded continuous functional calculus. Sharp indicator functions require separate boundary arguments.

slides.title: Unitary groups from diagonal phases
slides.lead: Bounded approximants can recover an unbounded unitary flow.
body: At each fixed time and for each fixed input, all phase multipliers have modulus one and converge coordinatewise; dominated convergence gives strong convergence of the unitary evolutions.

slides.title: A spectral projection counterexample
slides.lead: Resolvents can converge while an indicator cutoff jumps.
body: Take A_n=1/n on a one-dimensional space and A=0. The spectral projection for (-infinity,0] is zero for every approximant and the identity for the limit.

slides.title: Continuity sets restore convergence
slides.lead: Discontinuities must have no limiting spectral mass.
body: The projection result requires a suitable boundary condition. Strong resolvent convergence controls continuous bounded spectral tests; jumps at eigenvalues need additional hypotheses.
slides.takeaway: Check the spectral boundary before passing to a sharp projection.
